[[File:Shimonomiya Chikatsu Jinja Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Torii|qq=}}]]
**Chikatsu Shrine** (近津神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Daigo, Ibaraki|en|Daigo, Ibaraki|qid=Q1346817|lt=Daigo, Ibaraki}}, {{ill|Kuji District, Ibaraki|en|Kuji District, Ibaraki|qid=Q1075212|lt=Kuji District}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|en|Ibaraki Prefecture|qid=Q83273|lt=Ibaraki Prefecture}}, Japan. It is considered a debated shrine under the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaishaqq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} system and was formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=}}. It is also commonly referred to as **Shimonomiya Chikatsu Shrine**.
== History ==
According to shrine tradition, it was established by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケルqq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}}, with the shrine buildings constructed in the 4th year of the {{ill|Keiun|en|Keiun|qid=Q428753|lt=Keiun era}} (707). During the {{ill|Kōhei|en|Kōhei|qid=Q1193572|lt=Kōhei era}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} donated 3,000 kanmon to the shrine.
== Shrine Grounds ==
* **Hoko-sugi (鉾スギ)** – A designated {{ill|Natural Monument of Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県指定天然記念物qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Natural Monument of Ibaraki Prefecture|qq=}}. This sacred tree is 43 meters tall with a trunk circumference of 9.6 meters and is estimated to be over 1,200 years old. It is believed to have been planted when the shrine was first established.

== Festivals and Rituals ==
; **Nakataue of Chikatsu Shrine**
: A rice planting festival held annually on the {{ill|Summer solstice|en|Summer solstice|qid=Q7603898|lt=summer solstice}}. It is said to have originated with rice offerings donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|en|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qid=Q1194944|lt=Tokugawa Mitsukuni}} during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, suggesting the ritual dates back to the mid-Edo period. Sacred ropes ({{ill|Shimenawa|en|Shimenawa|qid=Q1887421|lt=shimenawa}}) are set around the rice fields, and after purification rites by the head priest, a group of young women (saotome) plant rice seedlings to the accompaniment of drums, flutes, and songs.
; **Omase Mawashi (御桝廻し)**
: An ancient ritual once practiced at the "Three Chikatsu Shrines" ({{ill|Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine|ja|馬場都々古別神社qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Yatsugi Tsutsukowake Shrine|ja|八槻都々古別神社qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yatsugi Tsutsukowake Shrine|qq=}}, and Shimonomiya Chikatsu Shrine) and later adopted by neighboring shrines. On October 28, a ritual rice measure (masu) filled with newly harvested rice is wrapped in straw matting and adorned with sacred wands (heisoku), then enshrined in a special hut. After seven years, it is passed to the next designated shrine with fresh rice.
These rituals reflect the shrine’s role as a guardian deity of agriculture, with similar practices found throughout {{ill|Daigo, Ibaraki|en|Daigo, Ibaraki|qid=Q1346817|lt=Daigo, Ibaraki}} and {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|en|Fukushima Prefecture|qid=Q71707|lt=Fukushima Prefecture}}, indicating a wide agricultural belief system spanning northern {{ill|Hitachi Province|en|Hitachi Province|qid=Q1055353|lt=Hitachi Province}} and southern {{ill|Mutsu Province|1=Mutsu Province|2=ja|3=陸奥国|ja|Mutsu Province|1=Mutsu Province|2=ja|3=陸奥国qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsu Province|qq=}}.
== Access ==
* A 5-minute walk from {{ill|Shimonomiya Station|en|Shimonomiya Station|qid=Q7497007|lt=Shimonomiya Station}} on the {{ill|Suigun Line|en|Suigun Line|qid=Q1056202|lt=Suigun Line}}, operated by {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East}}.
